$description:
Semantic tier, light theme. This file defines the key space every other theme must match — a theme missing a key here is a build error, because a brand that forgets to define `status.critical` must fail the build rather than render the default green.

Components reference these and only these.
$comment-border-strong: Backs --ox-field-border and --ox-chart-axis, both UI components under WCAG 1.4.11. slate.300 measured 1.48:1 on white — half the 3:1 floor. slate.500 is 4.76:1.

text-on-fill.$description: A label on a filled neutral — the Switch's off track, which is {border-strong} in every theme and therefore a mid-grey in every theme. Separate from text-on-accent because that one follows the accent, and the dark accent is light: pointing the off label at it put #071014 on #5d6c7e at 3.57:1. White clears AA on border-strong in all three themes, and the pair is in the contrast gate so it stays that way.

$comment-accent: White text on brand.600 measured 3.81:1, below the 4.5:1 floor for --ox-text-on-accent — that is every primary button label. brand.700 is 5.56:1.
$comment-focus-ring: brand.500 measured 2.50:1 on white against the 3:1 floor in SC 1.4.11 and 2.4.11 — the focus indicator for every interactive component in the library. brand.600 is 3.81:1 and stays distinct from the accent.

status.$description:
Clinical status. Paired with an icon and a text label in every component — these colours are reinforcement, not the signal.

`high` and `low` are separated by HUE rather than intensity, so the direction of an abnormal result survives monochrome printing and the common forms of colour vision deficiency.

critical.$description: red-700, not red-600: at 600 this was 4.41:1 on its own background — under the 4.5:1 floor by a hair. This is the single most consequential token in the library; it does not get to be borderline.

high.$description: amber-700, not amber-600: at 600 this was 3.07:1 on its own background. Amber is the hardest hue to keep accessible on a light surface and must be darkened further than the others to clear 4.5:1.

normal.$description: green-700, not green-600: at 600 this was 3.57:1 on its own background, below the AA floor. A status badge that fails contrast is a status badge some readers cannot read.

unknown.$description: Absence of interpretation is a distinct state from normal, and it gets its own colour so it cannot be mistaken for one.

recording.$description: The capture tell. The one red in the system that is not an alarm: fifty years of cameras, tape decks and voice-memo apps have made a red dot mean recording, and fighting that convention costs more than the collision does. Deliberately one step off status.critical rather than equal to it, so an alert raised DURING a capture is still the more urgent thing on screen — the pair is checked against each other, not only against the background.

flag.$description: Record-level flags. These describe the record, not the measurement, which is why they sit outside the status scale.

swatch.$description: Decorative only. Never the sole carrier of identity, and never mapped to any attribute of the person.
